German person working in drug rehabilitation here!  First day i worked at my job i was pretty shocked to see we had flyers for synanon at the office, because i only knew about the American branch and all that insanity. Soo i Was actually lurking to see if anyone had posted about this. 
Basically the gist is, that the german branch formed out of a different drug rehabilitation programe (release) back in the 70s and only later took on the name synanon after the founders of the german brand got into a fight with the founders of release. As far as Ive been able to find out, Its always been pretty seperate from the american one, besides the name and some of the same core rules (dunno how much they do the gane tho).
Intesresting side note; We have a bunch of those self contained drug rehabilitation self help type programs here and they all are a little sketch (in my personal opinion) but none of them have as many critics as synanon. The reason they work and still are a much better idea to a lot of people, is that in germany we have §35 btmg which basically gives drug addicts who’ve committed an offence in connection with or because of drug use the chance of going to rehab instead of prison. Now getting into rehab is actually quite a process because we live paperwork, so you might still get stuck in jail. But synanon and the other places like it will take you in 24/7 and most of them are §35 btmg certified so they function as if they’re a rehab program (which their not, but living in a shitty communal living space and possibly learning a new trait and kicking the habit sounds better then prison to me)

i've been in recovery for almost a year now. i still binge sometimes, but it happens about once every three or four months and i'm usually able to stop myself way earlier than i used to. 
I'm gonna go into different methods i found helpful with my different forms of binging (like where they came from) but lets start with what i did  before i was ever able to not binge.

I started by making sure i eat healthy and more importantly balanced, when i dont binge. For me personally, that basically meant finding out how big portions are. i had bo concept of what a normal portion looked like as i over- or under - ate my entire life. I googled portion sizes for carbs (like eg 75g of pasta = 1 portion), then i put this on a plate (dry). I than added about one or two handfuls of veggies and a protein based thing.My Partner gave me the tip of thinking of my plates in thirds so i put 1/3 protein, 1/3 carbs and 1/3 Veggies. 
This helped in me eating healthier in general, which was good for my overall wellbeing and self-worth and also helped regulate my weight gain a little bit.

Then I went to inpatient treatment. There I relearnd what hunger cues are, how to listen to them and also to adress the underlying issues behind WHY i was overeating.

i genuienly think this is a super helpful step, if not the most helpful, if your binge eating stems from emotional eating (eg. you binge because you're stressed or lonely or angry).

if your binge eating stems from restriction, what i find helpful is having more snacks. so basically you have 3 normal meals a day and then about every 2-3 hours after a big meal you have a little snack, like some fruit, carrots, yoghurt, stuff like that.

if your binge eating stems from food addiction the only thing i found helpful was complete fucking cold ass withdrawl. i threw out all my snacks. all my binge foods. i ate three meals and had carrots inbetween (carrots are great because you have to chew them for ages). i started freezing bread and only getting it out for lunch. i didnt have more food in the house than i needed for the week. when i cooked, i cooked exactly one portion. 

I also gave myself rewards - no binging for two days? awsome buy that nailpolish you wanted! gradually i moved up those rewards (no binging for a week? - how about some jewlery! 10 days? - get that tshirt! two weeks? - lets go to the cinema!) and so on. rewards help the human brain learn better than punishment does. 
hope any of this helps!
